note: The game UI's style table (Core/include/ftcore/UiStyle.h). Colours are sRGB hex. Text px are at 1080p before the player's text scale; nothing draws below min_text_px at 1080p or min_text_px_absolute at any height. Import checks contrast on the backing over a white picture that text on its hairline edge reads 4.5:1 over white, and that danger, ally and weak_point each have their own cue shape. The look is this table plus the stroke painters (Core UiStroke). Each world has its own ink and accent. The unwritten ink is a cold grey and its ink_dim is scaled from it as the other worlds' are (luminance x 0.6975); its accent is the ink itself (the prompt glyph's ring), and its backing and ally are cold neutrals. A value line's fill is the world's own fill token (2026-11-16: Solhaven parchment, Lattice cyan, Unwritten grey; white in high contrast), its track the world's backing at 0.45 with the track token as a 1 px top hairline, and its end a square ink cap lines.cap_grow px wider than the line (none on the dotted guard: lines.guard_dot dots at lines.guard_pitch). Danger is red in every world, its tone per world (Solhaven E60012, lattice D40010, unwritten C9000E; the hit cue is the unwritten red everywhere): red means harm to the player (the hit cue, the lost hp, the low underline, the call triangle) and nothing else; each colour-vision palette moves danger to luminance about 0.125 at its own hue, one colour for every world. The weak point is Mark (pale gold) in every world. The red fails the text rule, so danger_underline (on in every world) draws a danger word in ink with the red as its underline, and import measures danger 3:1 against the track body's colour, the ink and the world's fill instead (the hit cue's red against every fill too; the lost hp meets the fill across a 1 px ink separator); marks_accent2 (off everywhere) would put accent2 on marks. A world that leaves either key out has it off. sig_pulse, sig_arcs and sig_margin_rule switch the three signature devices (the Release pulse, ring arcs, the margin rule; margin_rule holds the rule's sizes): off in every world until the owner picks, and a pick flips one row. load_breaks (on in Solhaven only, 2026-11-16) puts short crosswise breaks in the Load's gold, so it reads apart from a warm hp fill by pattern, not colour; the gold stays one colour everywhere. special_prompt (on in every world, the owner's pick C, 2026-11-17) reserves the fight HUD's special prompt row (Core UiSpecial.h) above the fight's own prompts and draws it while the lead's special is ready; off, the prompt stack is as it was. special holds the choices still open with the owner (the Third called from the row, the Third acting himself, a mark for a ready partner), all off. The other lattice and unwritten values are provisional until those worlds' UI passes.
